title: 60s Inference Qualification Framework (seller quick-deck)
content:
Objective: Give field sellers a compact, repeatable 60-second qualification and a short slide deck they can run through during discovery calls. This is designed for quick live demos and to seed follow-ups with technical teams.

Slide 1 — Hook (10s):
- One-liner: “Redwood helps teams get predictable, low-latency LLM inference with enterprise controls — without building an inference stack.”
- Quick value bullets (spoken, not read): predictability, economics, and fallbacks for production.

Slide 2 — 60s Qualification Script (read-aloud):
- "Quick question set to see if Redwood is worth a deeper call: 1) Do you need sub-150ms median responses for customer-facing flows? 2) Are you on a crypto/PII-sensitive workflow that requires private deployment or KMS? 3) Do you expect bursty traffic >5x baseline within a week (pilot scale)? 4) Do you need token-level cost visibility and per-route SLOs?"
- Dealer notes: if they say yes to 1 and any of 2–4, escalate to AE-Technicals.

Slide 3 — Fast Tech Check (30s):
- Run these two probes on a discovery call: 1) Ask for current request counts per minute and percentiles for latency (p50/p95). 2) Confirm hosting constraints: cloud only vs VPC/on-prem.
- If they can only answer vaguely, propose a 15-min technical intake to gather telemetry.

Slide 4 — Seller Objection Snippets (for spoken rebuttal):
- "We have our own infra": "Totally — many platform teams keep infra but want unified SLOs, cost controls, and DR/fallbacks; Redwood can sit as a control plane and/or take dedicated pools so you don’t reimplement batching/kv caching."
- "Open models are cheaper": "Open models plus production-grade serving are nontrivial; Redwood’s runtime reduces per-token cost via batching, KV caching, and quantization guidance — we measure unit economics for you."

Slide 5 — Short Demo Script (3-minute):
- 0:00–0:30: Signpost: show Console -> model catalog (point to verified perf tags).
- 0:30–1:30: Send a sample chat request and show streaming tokens + p50/p95 live.
- 1:30–2:30: Flip to rollouts: show canary policy, automatic fallback to a cheaper variant.
- 2:30–3:00: Show cost breakdown for that request and the token-level trace.

Slide 6 — Rapid Qualification Matrix (spoken decision tree):
- If sub-150ms SLO & security requirement -> path: Private deployment or Dedicated + KMS.
- If latency tolerant (>300ms) & cost-sensitive -> path: Hosted API + quantization recommendations.
- If bursty, unpredictable load -> path: Dedicated with burst pool + autoscale policy.

Slide 7 — Economic Quick Numbers (benchmarks to cite):
- Small chat session (avg 125 tokens): hosted median cost example $0.006 — Dedicated optimized ~25–40% lower depending on batching.
- Embedding batch (1000 vectors): hosted vs dedicated delta, call out cache opportunities.
- Use phrasing: "estimates only — propose a short econ intake to produce customer-specific numbers."

Slide 8 — Hand-off checklist for AE+SE pairing (post-meeting):
- Capture sample prompt set + 3 real traces or representative telemetry.
- Capture target SLOs (p50/p95, tail budget), budget constraints, and data residency needs.
- Request a Slack thread + Confluence artifact for intake.

Slide 9 — Follow-up templates (copy-paste):
- Quick follow: "Thanks — great convo. Next step: 15-min tech intake to collect traces and target SLOs. Proposed times: [slot1]/[slot2]."
- Technical ask: "Please share 3 sample request traces (JSON) or cloud metrics for 48–72h covering peak and baseline windows."

Slide 10 — Field tips & danger signs (speaker notes):
- Danger sign: customer says "we only care about accuracy" and cannot articulate latency/cost; push to product owner and probe for user-facing flows.
- Tip: When platform engineers are present, avoid pricing until you have traces (reduces back-and-forth).

Appendix — Quick rebut matrices (cheat sheet lines):
- Reliability concern -> show fallback & canary flow + SLA language.
- Cost pushback -> offer an A/B test: same prompt, quantized variant vs baseline, measure latency & cost delta.

Appendix — Next steps checklist for seller: 30/60/90 day play:
- 0–30d: Run tech intake, gather traces, baseline demos.
- 30–60d: Pilot (hosted) with cost/latency tracking or Dedicated reserved capacity planning.
- 60–90d: Rollout plan, SLOs codified, and optional private deployment discussions.

Notes to self (author):
- Need a short slide graphic for "fallback flow" and one for "cost delta visualization".
- Pair with an AE/SE roleplay video — ask Maya to record simple 4-min roleplay.
- Iterate after a batch of 10 pilot conversations to collect language that resonates.

End of deck — attachments: 1) 15-min intake form (confluence link in linked_artifacts), 2) brief ROI worksheet (CSV), 3) sample telemetry JSON schema.
